value_text: With US managed APIs unavailable under sanctions, self-hosted open-weight models are the only path that does not depend on a foreign provider relationship. Chinese-origin weights dominate the accessible set on licence and capability grounds.
source_notes: Structural inference from the sanctions posture in countries.json and the licence terms in models.json, not a usage measurement. Dated to the DeepSeek-R1 release, which materially changed what was available under a permissive licence.

value_text: Any managed AI access is mediated by circumvention infrastructure, making it contingent on censorship conditions rather than on provider terms alone.
source_notes: Qualitative framing only. The measured version of this signal is produced at runtime by the OONI and Tor Metrics fetchers into technology_blocks, blocking_timeline, and tor_metrics; this row records the structural claim, not the measurement.

value_text: Formal sanctions relief did not restore managed API adoption, because payment rails, KYC checks, and provider geo-blocking were built around the prior posture and lag the legal change.
source_notes: Matches the POST_SANCTIONS_LAG reasoning in engine/rules.rs. Dated to the effective date of the revocation order. This is the gap the tool exists to make visible: legal status and practical access are not the same variable.

value_text: A state-linked entity publishes an Arabic-first open-weight model family, giving the UAE a domestic option that does not require a foreign provider relationship even while it sits inside the US compute stack.
source_notes: Corresponds to the jais-30b row in models.json. Confidence MEDIUM on the date, matching that row. Illustrates the model-layer hedging that engine/rules.rs describes for US_COMPUTE_STACK countries.

value_text: A state-owned vehicle now holds national compute procurement, giving Saudi Arabia a single counterparty for accelerator and cloud agreements rather than fragmented ministry-level buying.
source_notes: Corresponds to the sa-humain-launch-2025 row in deals.json. Confidence MEDIUM on exact date.

value_text: No bilateral compute pathway comparable to the Gulf arrangements exists. Small open-weight models on locally-owned hardware are the only route that avoids both cost and payment friction.
source_notes: Structural inference, not a measurement: the absence of any IQ row in deals.json is itself the evidence. Dated against the Gulf frameworks it is being contrasted with. Matches the RESOURCE_CONSTRAINED reasoning in engine/rules.rs.
